solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lied, with fibs broadcast, skewered by European scepticism

indicators.note: Scattered widely, so the letters are strewn about
The letters are run through by the skewer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: A fibbing speaker is met with doubt from a Eurosceptic audience.
explanation.walkthrough: "with" just joins LIED to FIBS as one batch of letters; the E then pierces them after DISB.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief is a refusal to accept something as true, which is scepticism.

clue.text: Fed up about American unwilling to listen

indicators.note: In a down clue, reading upwards turns the word round
Around, so FED wraps the A

explanation.surface: Someone is sick of a stubborn American who won't hear them out.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fed up" reads as one idiom meaning annoyed; split it, and "up" turns FED over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in its figurative sense: someone who will not heed what is said is deaf, whatever their hearing.

clue.text: Jabber "Yes", startled to receive piece of jewellery

indicators.note: Jolted out of order, so the letters are shaken up
The shaken letters take the jewellery inside them

explanation.surface: Someone blurts out "Yes!" in shock on being handed a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: "Jabber" looks like a verb for chattering; it is a noun, the thing that jabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A syringe delivers a jab, so it is literally a jabber.

clue.text: One is cycling for a long time

indicators.note: Going round, so the last letter comes round to the front

parts.note: ONE with its E moved to the front

explanation.surface: Someone has been out on a bike for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling moves letters from one end to the other without changing their order; the E at the end comes round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an eon is an age, a span of time too long to measure comfortably.

clue.text: One's unusual menu is not susceptible to complaint?

indicators.note: Out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner with an odd menu refuses to listen to grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: "complaint" means an illness here, not a grumble, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone immune cannot catch a disease, and a complaint is an ailment.

clue.text: Infallible dessert, with a measure of alcoholic content

parts.note: A fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding
Proof is the strength scale for spirits

explanation.surface: A pudding that can't go wrong, especially with a boozy kick.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream, as in gooseberry fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foolproof cannot fail, so it is infallible.

clue.text: Soldier dismissing odd parts in poem

indicators.note: Throwing out letters 1, 3, 5 and so on leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: An army discharges its misfits to write verse.
explanation.walkthrough: "odd parts" sounds like strange bits; it means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the ode is one kind of poem, a formal lyric addressed to its subject, like Keats's odes.

clue.text: Oxford college that is in the care of old hands?

parts.note: Right hand, the first of the two

explanation.surface: An Oxford college is looked after by its veteran staff.
explanation.walkthrough: "old hands" reads as experienced people; split it into O plus the two hands, R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Oriel, founded in 1326, is one particular college within Oxford University.

clue.text: A lot of poetry in Old English, revolutionary to a large extent

indicators.note: Most but not all, so the last letter goes
Turned right round, so OE flips

parts.note: VERSE losing its last letter, placed inside EO

explanation.surface: Much old English verse was radical in a big way.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the Old English is turned; VERS sits inside it after the flip.
explanation.definitionFit: "Ever so" means very much, as in ever so grateful.

clue.text: Scuba, say, friend puts on in the morning

indicators.note: The friend is placed inside the morning

explanation.surface: A friend gets dressed in diving gear early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: "Scuba" pictures diving, but SCUBA stands for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: SCUBA is formed from initial letters, which makes it an acronym.

clue.text: Suppose unity encompasses mathematical ratio

parts.note: Circumference to diameter, placed inside ONE

explanation.surface: A mathematician speculates about the number one containing a famous ratio.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, about 3.14.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to opine is to put forward a view, which is what supposing something out loud amounts to.

clue.text: US city laid in pianos for distribution

indicators.note: To be handed out, so the letters are spread around

explanation.surface: An American city has stocked up on pianos to hand out.
explanation.walkthrough: All of "laid in pianos" is the fodder, every letter used once.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Indianapolis, capital of Indiana and home of the Indy 500, is one American city.

clue.text: International traveller, first to Tunis, is one less interested in the wider world

definitions.text: one less interested in the wider world

indicators.note: Take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A globetrotter heads first to Tunis, yet turns out to care little for the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes a traveller the opposite of the answer; the joke is that the rover is inside the introvert.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert turns inward and cares less for the outside world.

clue.text: Busy insect beginning to taste vegetable

indicators.note: Take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A bee starts sampling a vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: "Busy" only picks out which insect; bees are proverbially busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: beet, as in beetroot or sugar beet, is a root crop eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Almost completed new kitchen feature

indicators.note: Not quite all, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A fitted kitchen is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: "completed" means OVER, as in the game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the oven is one of the fixed appliances that make up a kitchen.

clue.text: With bathroom unfortunately in use, heads for the exit

indicators.note: Things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled
Take the first letter of each following word

parts.note: First letters of THE and EXIT, added to the mix

explanation.surface: The bathroom is occupied, so someone gives up and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: "heads for the exit" reads as leaving; it only supplies T and E to join IN USE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite room has its own bathroom attached.

clue.text: Church using speech and using singers

parts.note: Relating to speech, spoken rather than written
Surface padding that echoes the definition; "speech" alone supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A church service mixes spoken words and a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival, matching an adjective answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written for a choir, so it uses singers.

clue.text: Directed to drop temperature? Get angry

explanation.surface: Someone told to turn the heating down loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: "Directed to drop temperature" reads as an instruction; it is STEERED with its T gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become suddenly furious.

clue.text: Change of ownership originally eliminating resistance steadily and quickly

explanation.surface: A company takeover quietly and rapidly squeezes out opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: "originally" looks like a first-letter signal; here it is simply FIRST, which then loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Making money hand over fist means earning it steadily and fast.

clue.text: Dark chesspiece hiding King

parts.note: The piece that moves in an L

explanation.surface: A black chess piece screens its own king.
explanation.walkthrough: "Dark" looks like it describes the chesspiece; it is the definition, as in after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in a noun sense: "dark" can mean the hours of darkness, as in out after dark.

clue.text: Try and learn

definitions.meaning: What a judge does with a case in court

explanation.surface: Advice to make an effort and study.
explanation.walkthrough: "Try" means to put on trial, not attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A court tries or hears a case, and to hear news is to learn it.

clue.text: Regret limiting attempt, after turning unpredictable

indicators.note: Once flipped, so GO is turned round

parts.note: GO, as in have a go, turned round

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for holding back an effort goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: "Limiting" means bordering on both sides, so RUE splits to hold the turned GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue element, like a rogue elephant, behaves erratically.

clue.text: Be exultant regarding Irish writer on the radio

parts.note: Re, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: Broadcast as sound, so only how it is said counts

explanation.surface: Delight at a radio programme about an Irish author.
explanation.walkthrough: James Joyce was the Irish author of Ulysses; only the sound of his name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy.

clue.text: Elation: Juliet and Romeo, finally, finally together

indicators.note: At the end, so the last letter is taken, of Romeo and of the word itself

explanation.surface: Delight as Shakespeare's lovers are at last united.
explanation.walkthrough: The second "finally" is its own fodder, giving its final Y. Juliet and Romeo pretend to be the lovers; Juliet is J in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy and elation both mean great happiness.

clue.text: Allowed lease

definitions.meaning: A tenancy of a property, British usage

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a let is a rental agreement for a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the past tense of permit, and a noun for a rental agreement.

clue.text: Cuddly toy to stand behind lingerie item

parts.note: To tolerate, as in can't stand it

explanation.surface: A soft toy is propped up behind some underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: "stand" means tolerate, not stay upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the stuffed bear named after Teddy Roosevelt is the archetypal cuddly toy.
